title: Two hamzas: the joining one and the cutting one

bigIdea.text: Hamza is a small catch in the throat, like the break in 'uh-oh'. The cutting hamza is always said. The joining hamza (ٱ) is said only when you start with it; in the middle of reading you glide straight past it.

proper.text: Hamzat al-qat' ('cutting hamza') is a real letter: a short closing of the throat, then its vowel. It is written ء, often on a seat: أ or إ on an alif, ؤ on a waw, ئ on a dotless ya-shape. Say it every time, at the start, middle or end of a word.
Hamzat al-wasl ('joining hamza') only comes at the start of a word. In this mushaf it is an alif with a small head and no vowel mark: ٱ.
When you read on from the word before, the joining hamza and its vowel drop out: go straight from the last vowel of the previous word to the next letter you pronounce.

When you START on ٱ (at the start of an ayah, or again after a stop), say it: with 'a' in 'al-' ('the'); in a verb, with 'u' if its third letter has a damma, otherwise with 'i'; in the few nouns that have it (such as the words for 'name' and 'son'), with 'i'. A few verbs are exceptions; Stage 2 covers them.
The app's colours grey out ٱ as silent everywhere except at the very start of an ayah: none of the 231 ayat that begin with ٱ have it greyed, because there you start with it and say it.

memoryHook.text: Joining hamza: say it to start, skip it to join. Cutting hamza: always say it.

extras.text: English has a hamza too: the catch in 'uh-oh', or at the start of 'apple' said sharply.
Persian/Urdu readers: ء and ع are different letters. Keep ء a light catch in the throat and ع a deeper squeeze from the middle of the throat.

note.text: Inside the ayah the ٱ of the second word is not said: go from the first word's kasra straight to the lam.
Joined reading: from the fatha at the end of the second word straight into the doubled lam.
Starting the ayah on 'al-': begin with 'a'.
Starting the ayah on ٱ in a verb: the third letter (د) has a kasra, so begin with 'i'.
Starting on ٱ in a verb whose third letter (ع) has a damma: begin with 'u'.
A cutting hamza on an alif (أ): always said.
A cutting hamza under the alif (إ): 'i'.
A cutting hamza in the middle of a word, on a ya-shaped seat (ئ).

tip.text: أَ: a light catch, then 'a'. عَ: squeeze the middle of the throat; the sound is deeper and has a slight strain.

remnote: Hamzat al-qat' (أ إ ء ؤ ئ) == Cutting hamza: always pronounced
Hamzat al-wasl (ٱ) == Joining hamza: said only when you start with it; skipped when you read on
Starting on ٱ == 'a' in al-; in verbs 'u' if the 3rd letter has a damma, else 'i'; nouns like 'name', 'son': 'i'
